answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes achieve consensus while 1,000 fakes stall at the memory island. A verifier challenges agents with random memory-access puzzles; failure to return data matching the terrace of required working sets triggers a penalty. This haven of strict hardware-bound latency mandates that each agent maintains unique bus access, preventing pooling. Honest participants pay 120 watts to maintain their status, whereas fakes incur costs that scale linearly per identity, rendering large farms inefficient.
